thread:
maria: Heads-up — us-west2 GPU pool is at ~95% allocation. Autoscaler attempted a resize but the GitOps/Helm rollout for `nodepool-resize` is blocked by the OPA freeze-window policy on premerge. We need a short, emergency exemption to run a targeted remediation rollout to avoid pod evictions and QoS drops.

maria: Proposed plan (short):
- Canary: resize 1/10 of nodes (min impact)
- Run smoke tests (kube-proxy / inference health) and observe latency for 10m
- If passed, continue remaining 90% in 2 batches with 5m watch windows
- If failed, immediate `helm rollback` + revert Terraform change

maria: I trimmed the terraform plan and helm diff below for reviewers. Requesting an OPA exemption for 30 minutes to perform the remediation. @jordan @ash @sre-oncall pls ack so I can file the exemption.

maria: ```
# terraform plan snippet
# module: nodepool
+ google_container_node_pool.resize (1 change)
size: 12 -> 16
```

ash: Are we sure this is a policy exemption and not something we can delay until the maintenance freeze ends? What is the user impact if we wait 2 hours?

maria: Waiting ~2h will start evicting best-effort pods on busy nodes (batch jobs + CI runners). Some internal eval jobs will OOM; risk to customer latency is low but increased noise and failed jobs for platform users. Not safe IMO.

jordan: I'm +1 for exemption if we keep it tightly scoped and add a smoke test. Can we attach an automated smoke test that fails the rollout early? If so I'll sign off here.

maria: Yes — plan is `kubectl run smoke-inference --image=internal/smoke:latest --timeout=2m` then hit /health and run a short generate with sample prompt. Failure criteria: >500ms median p95 or any 500 response.

ash: Also require a CI gate: block merge if helm diff includes more than nodepool changes. Are we only changing nodepool size?

maria: Only nodepool size + labels for scheduling. No workload changes. Helm chart diff: nodePool.replicas: 12 -> 16.

policy-bot: OPA premerge check: denied (rule: freeze-window). To request a temporary exemption use: https://redwood.example.com/opa/exemptions/new — include mitigation steps and sign-offs.

maria: Filed exemption request: https://redwood.example.com/opa/exemptions/4321 — notes: canary=10%, smoke-tests=yes, owner=maria, requested_duration=30m.

ops-bot: @maria created exemption 4321 — status: pending approvals (need 2 approvals: infra-lead + oncall). Link: https://redwood.example.com/opa/exemptions/4321

sre-oncall: I'm oncall and will monitor. I'll approve if we keep canary + automated smoke and a watch officer for 30m. I'll be online for the window.

jordan: Approved — condition: add a prometheus alert to the exemption (p95 latency > 350ms) and auto-rollback hook.

ash: Approved from infra side. Keep the window < 45m and notify #incidents if anything spikes. :thumbsup:

policy-bot: Exemption 4321 approved by: [jordan, ash, sre-oncall]. Expires in 40m. Audit: https://redwood.example.com/opa/exemptions/4321/audit

maria: Starting canary now. Command: ```helm upgrade nodepool-release ./charts/nodepool --set nodePool.replicas=16 --wait --timeout 10m```

ops-bot: Canary rollout started for nodepool-release (canary 10%). Monitoring hooks: smoke-test job queued.

maria: smoke-test passed (latency p95 220ms). Proceeding to next batch in 5m.

ops-bot: Rollout completed. No elevated error rates. Reverting exemption will be automated at expiry.

maria: Thanks all — closing the loop. Will attach postmortem summary to the exemption ticket later.
